tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent (assessing/auditing security posture, asking about guardrails/encryption/logging), explicitly lists trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name a specific control, and remains a concise paragraph.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when the user wants to assess, audit, or review the security posture of Amazon Bedrock generative-AI workloads... Apply it even when the user does not name a specific control, for example when they ask whether their Bedrock guardrails, knowledge bases, agents, or custom models are set up securely..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (e.g., what IAM or encryption is) and sticks to project-specific scope boundaries, safety rules, and procedural steps the agent wouldn't otherwise know (e.g., the bedrock vs bedrock-agent SDK distinction, verify-vs-prescribe contract). It is dense but every section carries non-obvious, skill-specific information.
tests.evidence: Mind the difference between the SDK client and the IAM action prefix: Bedrock prompts, agents, knowledge bases, flows, and agent action groups are called through the bedrock-agent SDK client ... but their IAM actions use the bedrock: prefix

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large reference tables, API docs, or error-code lists are embedded in the body; detailed check logic is deferred to references/bedrock-checks.md and referenced conditionally rather than inlined into decision branches.
tests.evidence: Open [references/bedrock-checks.md](references/bedrock-checks.md) and execute every check. Each entry gives the read-only API call(s), the pass/fail/N-A logic, severity, verifiability, resolution text...

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Both files in references/ (bedrock-checks.md and finding-schema-and-report.md) are linked with markdown link syntax multiple times in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is tied to a specific workflow step with clear context on when to load it (e.g., resolving regions, running checks, assembling report), not a generic 'see for details' mention.
tests.evidence: See [references/finding-schema-and-report.md](references/finding-schema-and-report.md) → "Region resolution". ... Open [references/bedrock-checks.md](references/bedrock-checks.md) and execute every check.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at the skill directory with no absolute paths or parent traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/safety-critical sections (read-only guardrail, verify-vs-prescribe contract, multi-region/account handling) are highly prescriptive with exact rules, while flexible sections (e.g., how to word findings, how to assemble report content) leave room for agent judgment. This matches fragility appropriately given it's a security assessment skill where false positives/negatives have real consequences.
tests.evidence: NEVER call any API that creates, updates, deletes, attaches, enables, disables, or otherwise mutates a resource... Emit N/A and put the recommended configuration in Resolution. Never emit Passed or Failed for a Prescribe-only check.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present competing tools/approaches as a menu; it specifies exact API clients and verbs to use (bedrock-agent vs bedrock) rather than offering multiple alternatives.
tests.evidence: Bedrock prompts, agents, knowledge bases, flows, and agent action groups are called through the bedrock-agent SDK client (e.g. bedrock-agent list_agents)

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (resolve scope, run checks per region/account, validate, report) applicable to any Bedrock environment, rather than hardcoding one specific instance's details.
tests.evidence:
- [ ] Step 1: Confirm intent and scope (read-only, accounts in scope)
- [ ] Step 2: Resolve target regions
- [ ] Step 3: Run every Bedrock check per region (BR-01..BR-31)

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes explicit, concrete pitfalls specific to this domain (SDK/IAM prefix mismatch causing false N/A, missing KMS key being AWS-owned not unencrypted, Prescribe-only check being wrongly marked Passed), functioning as a gotchas section even without that exact heading.
tests.evidence: Using the bedrock client for those resources yields a false N/A... A missing modelKmsKeyArn or serverSideEncryptionConfiguration is reported as "AWS-owned key", never as "unencrypted".
